paper.title: Scalable Ground-State Certification of Quantum Spin Systems via Structured Noncommutative Polynomial Optimization (Wang, Jansen, Frérot, Renou, Magron, Acín, 2026)

method.note: QMBCertify.jl builds a semidefinite program whose optimum is a provable lower bound on the ground-state energy (the dual of a variational method: it squeezes $E_0$ from below, never above). It hard-codes the Heisenberg model's symmetries (translation, dihedral, $xyz$ permutation, sign, conjugate) to block-diagonalize the SDP. Relaxation order $d=4$ is the accuracy dial — the paper's own 2D value. All strengthening constraints (RDM positivity, state optimality) are off, matching the paper's official 2D example. Mosek 11 is the commercial SDP solver (free academic license).

params.name: relaxation order $d$
params.why: the reproduction value; the bound tightens monotonically in $d$
params.risk: too small $d$ → bound visibly looser than Table 8; too large → SDP out of memory
params.fix: if the bound misses the paper value, first check solver status/residuals, then consider $d$ escalation at L=4 only

params.name: strengthenings (rdm / pso / lso)
params.why: 2D scalability comes from symmetry block-diagonalization, not strengthenings; the paper uses them mainly for 1D chains
params.risk: turning them on inflates the SDP; a deviation from the paper changes the expected numbers
params.fix: keep off; revisit only as an opt-in verification experiment

params.name: long-range basis reach (extra)
params.why: matches the paper's 2D monomial basis at this target
params.risk: a larger extra changes the basis and hence the bound

params.name: system sizes $L$
params.source: track scope (tracks/polyopt/README.md); paper goes to L=16
params.why: beginner tier: the three sizes with published ED/QMC reference values; L=8 is the heaviest point a 54 GB workstation can plausibly attempt
params.risk: L=8 may hit the memory wall (paper used a 1 TB machine for L=16)
params.fix: assemble-first block-statistics check before each solve; if L=8 exceeds local memory, move that one point to the cluster via /using-slurm

params.name: reference values
params.value: paper Table 8 verbatim: ED for L=4,6; QMC for L=8
params.source: paper Table 8 (line-verbatim from the rendered text)
params.why: the reproduction target; recomputing 6x6 ED (9 billion-dimensional sector) is out of beginner scope
params.risk: none scientific — the sandwich check E_SDP ≤ E_ref still validates the run
params.fix: optional L=4 own-ED cross-check available as an opt-in verification

params.name: SDP solver
params.source: QMBCertify hard dependency; smoke-tested 2026-07-27 (chain N=4, d=2 bound = -0.49999999 vs exact -0.5)
params.risk: a stalled or infeasible solver status silently invalidates the certificate
params.fix: accept only a clean OPTIMAL status; quote digits at the residual level

estimate.memory: tens of GB — the risk point

risks: L=8 memory wall — assemble-first block check before paying for the solve
solver status must be clean OPTIMAL; stalled = no certificate
trustworthy digits are capped by solver residuals, not printed decimals

figures.plots: certified lower bound on $E_0/N$ vs $L$, beside the paper's reference (ED/QMC) values

observe.quantity: SDP optimum = certified lower bound on the ground-state energy per spin
observe.normalization: per spin ($E/N$), with $S = \sigma/2$ so $H = \sum S_i \cdot S_j = \frac{1}{4} \sum \sigma_i \cdot \sigma_j$

figures.expected: E_SDP/N ≤ E_ref/N at every L (the sandwich), and agreement with the paper's Table 8 values (-0.701783, -0.680886, -0.676370) to solver precision; reproduced = all three bounds below their references and matching the paper

numbers.L=6: ours -0.684605 (extra=0) -> -0.683172 with extra=7 = paper old [31] (6 digits) | paper new -0.680886 | ref (ED) -0.678872

results.why: the certification pipeline is fully validated (all bounds sit below their ED/QMC references, Mosek OPTIMAL, residuals ~1e-7) and the run EXACTLY reproduces the paper's OLD [31] column — L=4 to 6 digits with the official example settings, L=6 to 6 digits once the full-range basis is used (extra=7). The NEW Table 8 column is not reachable with any shipped setting (a full knob sweep: SU2, rdm=8, lso, pso, extra — closes only part of the gap): the public repo implements the 2024 PRX relaxation (its README cites only that paper), while the 2026 paper's new structured reductions that produce the new column are not yet released in the code. Root cause, not a numerical fluke.
results.wall: 27 s + 49 s + 231 s (L = 4, 6, 8), solver status OPTIMAL at every size
